articles.title: Amazon’s new Kindle Colorsoft is a premium e-reader with a premium price | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The latest model is lighter and thinner than its predecessor and features an edge-to-edge display. But if you already own the first-generation Colorsoft, there’s little reason to upgrade.
articles.body_text: Amazon recently unveiled its refreshed Kindle lineup , introducing a new basic Kindle , Paperwhite, and Colorsoft. The new Kindle Colorsoft starts at $290, while the Signature Edition, which I’ve spent the past few weeks testing, costs $320. The base model comes with 16GB of storage, while the Signature Edition doubles that to 32GB and is available in graphite or a maroon-like Fig finish with an aluminum back. Amazon first brought color to its Kindle lineup in 2024 with the launch of the original Colorsoft. The latest model is lighter and thinner than its predecessor and features an edge-to-edge display. If you already own the first-generation Colorsoft, there’s little reason to upgrade. The core reading experience remains largely the same. Both models have a 7-inch color E-Ink display, 300ppi resolution for black-and-white content and 150ppi for color. However, if you’ve been eyeing a color e-reader, the new Colorsoft is worth considering if you can get past the hefty price tag. Unlike standard Kindles, which display everything in black and white, the Colorsoft brings your digital bookshelf to life with their original colors. This makes it a particularly appealing option for readers who enjoy comics, graphic novels, or cookbooks, where color makes a big difference. It’s also great for readers who like highlighting passages in different colors. It’s worth noting that colors on the Colorsoft are still relatively muted and not as vibrant as what you’d see on an iPad. Still, they add a welcome splash of color and make a noticeable difference compared to the black-and-white displays of standard Kindles. The Colorsoft lets you adjust the screen’s color temperature, so you can switch to a warmer, more yellow-toned display that’s easier on the eyes when reading at night. There’s also an auto-adjusting brightness option that comes in handy. When it comes to battery life, Amazon says that the Colorsoft can last up to eight weeks on a single charge, compared to up to 12 weeks for the Paperwhite. During my testing, I didn’t have to stress about charging the Colorsoft because like other Kindles, its battery lasts a relatively long time compared to other everyday electronics. One small but welcome improvement on the new Colorsoft is the repositioned power button. On the previous generation, it was on the bottom of the device next to the charging port, making it easy to accidentally press it when handling the Kindle. On the new model, Amazon has moved it to the top-right edge, where it’s less likely to get in the way. I quite like this change, and found the new location more intuitive when powering the device on and off. I enjoyed the premium feel of the aluminum back on the Signature Edition. Although Amazon provided a case with my review unit, I rarely used it, and the finish held up well. While the slimmer design isn’t a major change, I found the new Colorsoft quite comfortable to hold compared to older Kindle devices. For those who enjoy reading in the bath or by the pool, the Colorsoft is waterproof, so you don’t have to worry about accidental splashes or spills damaging the e-reader.

articles.title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia poured tens of billions into AI startups under Huang. Without him at the helm, founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations.
articles.body_text: It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down . “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news. Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor , pouring tens of billions into startups annually and participating in 105 rounds this year alone, often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital. Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition. “Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamillah Bankiya told TechCrunch. Most of the significant decisions to invest in startups often came from Jensen himself, according to Umesh Padval, managing partner at Seligman Ventures. Padval has known Huang since serving on the board of Mellanox Technologies, a networking chipmaker Nvidia acquired for approximately $7 billion in 2020. While there is hope that Huang’s eventual successor will resume his dealmaking spree, investors aren’t hopeful that it will happen in the short term. Nvidia’s interim CEO, Colette Kress, is expected to institute some changes , especially when it comes to Nvidia’s investments into AI startups at the crux of the billion-dollar data center build-out . Huang’s rampant dealmaking in this sphere has been a source of concern for Wall Street. “She’s much more conservative,” one investor said of Kress. “I don’t think she’s going to commit the same amount of money to keep the early-stage ecosystem going.” Nvidia’s biggest bets were backing neoclouds, inference providers, and open weight models, which are expensive for smaller companies to build. “Jensen’s initiatives are a big reason an ecosystem has emerged despite that,” Zain Javaid, co-founder of the hardware company Ghost, said. For instance, Nvidia backed CoreWeave when it was still private and participated in two of Crusoe’s rounds, including its $1.4 billion Series E. It bought Hugging Face this year for $13 billion (expected to close in 2027) and holds investments in Mistral AI, Lambda, and Black Forest Labs. Nvidia was often the largest investor in the deals. Last year, it wrote an $800 million check into a $2 billion Series B round for Reflection AI, before the open source startup began to earn meaningful revenue, according to the Wall Street Journal . “Jensen believed in open source and frankly speaking, Europe,” Bankiya said of how Huang invested so much in AI across the world. The cease of that support in other regions outside of America, like Europe “would be a massive funding and honestly ecosystem gap that no one can fill.” It’s also true that Nvidia was such a dominant player in the ecosystem that at times, it felt like a monopoly. By backing so many companies with such generous checks, Nvidia effectively locked those startups into using its chips, which helped reinforce its dominant market position. If the company does grow more conservative with its startup investments, that could leave more room for rivals and smaller competitors. (Coincidentally, Google announced two new chips this week amid Huang’s Nvidia fallout.)

articles.title: US government grounds all flights across the United States 'due to extraordinary circumstances' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: A spokesperson for the FAA told TechCrunch that it issued the ground stop "following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers," which manage the airspace across the United States.
articles.body_text: The Federal Aviation Administration said Friday afternoon that it has grounded all flights across the United States due to “extraordinary circumstances” and issues related to safety. The FAA’s website said the cause is an “equipment outage.” The site itself was down for a brief period at the time of publication, with a note that the website was “experiencing technical difficulties.” Per an alert sent by the Air Traffic Control System Command Center , or ATCSCC, the FAA said the ground stop means that aircraft cannot take off from departure gates. The message said that the disruption was “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” but did not specify further. The alert was not visible on the ATCSCC website at press time. The alert stated that all departing flights must remain on the ground “until further notice.” Inbound international flights will be “managed on a case-by-case basis,” it said. A spokesperson for the FAA told TechCrunch that it issued the ground stop “following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” which manage the airspace across the United States. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X : “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.” It’s not clear what caused the ongoing FAA equipment outage. The outage comes in the same week that the administration rolled out an AI-powered tool for air traffic controllers to save aircraft flight time and fuel costs — though it’s unclear if the ongoing outage is related. Speaking to reporters outside the White House, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that there is “no indication yet that this was a nefarious act,” but warned that the recovery “is going to take some time.” Updated with comment from the FAA, and remarks from Homeland Security. articles.title: Exclusive: This young startup wants to power floating data centers with the ocean’s heat, and investors are already on board | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Drogue is harvesting heat from the ocean to power data centers on floating vessels. The first prototype should be bobbing around the ocean, crunching bits, in less than two years.
articles.body_text: Anyone who has weathered a hurricane can tell you that the oceans — which fuel the storms — contain a tremendous amount of energy. Thanks to global warming, they’re holding more than ever. A new startup wants to harness that energy to power data centers. Drogue , which has kept a low profile until now, is building a system that harvests heat from the ocean to power data centers on board floating vessels. According to founder and CEO Sam Sipe, the first prototype should be bobbing around the ocean, crunching bits, less than two years from now. The goal, Sipe said, is to help data center developers deploy servers in AI-friendly timelines. “The data center industry is a real estate game, and so they’re playing on 8- to 10-year timelines, including interoperability with utilities and [independent system operators]” that manage regional power grids, he said. “AI demand has increased 10x in just the last three years. It’s completely incompatible.” Drogue was founded just six months ago in Washington, D.C., and the startup told TechCrunch exclusively that it has already raised $20 million, including from XYZ Venture Capital, Toyota Ventures, Tamarack Global, Dream, FDVC, Garuda Ventures, Flexcap, Boost VC, and Slow Ventures, among other investors. In those six months, Drogue has designed a multi-megawatt prototype that will be installed on a traditional oceangoing ship and sent out to sea in early 2028. Future versions will be built on floating structures that more closely resemble offshore oil platforms. To Sipe, the decision to turn to the ocean was obvious. After years flying E-2D Hawkeyes off U.S. Navy aircraft carriers, he had an appreciation for the ocean’s immense power. “Most people think, oh, ocean — hard waves, storms, corrosion, biofouling. And I just see this majestic place and resource that we just ignore,” he said. As the planet warms, the oceans have been absorbing an additional 5.8 million terawatt-hours of energy every year. By comparison, all of human civilization uses about 180,000 terawatt-hours each year. If Drogue were to take some, surely the ocean wouldn’t miss it. The startup’s technology works like a heat pump run in reverse. A heat pump uses electricity to move heat from one place to another; Drogue’s system instead uses a difference in temperature to generate electricity. This approach, known as ocean thermal energy conversion, or OTEC, was first developed in the 1950s. Surface waters are warmer, heated by the sun, while down-deep temperatures are much colder, about 39°F on average (4°C). “There’s basically no amount of heat we can pull out of that that will collapse that temperature differential,” Sipe said. To leverage the temperature differential, the startup’s system draws in warm surface water, uses it to cool the data centers, and then sends the now-warmer water to boil ammonia, a chemical that turns to gas at -28°F. That ammonia gas is then sent through a turbine to generate electricity. Once through the turbine, it courses through a condenser, which turns the gas back into a liquid. There, cold water drawn from 1,000 meters deep passes over the condenser’s fins to absorb the heat. The warmed water is then released, and dissipates into the ocean. The ammonia gets sent back to the start of the sealed loop, and the cycle repeats.

articles.title: ChatGPT's new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you | TechCrunch
articles.summary: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out on users' behalf, starting with a limited rollout to U.S. Pro subscribers.
articles.body_text: OpenAI says that users are fully in control of the purchases, as they’re able to review the items, the total, and the payment card that will be used to complete the transaction before the checkout occurs. In addition, users will approve the purchases directly with a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint, which creates a record of their transaction. The addition comes as consumer-facing AI tools are working to find the right product-market fit, in terms of how they can help people be more efficient as they complete various tasks. While companies like DoorDash and Uber have so far reported low numbers of orders placed by AI agents, Meta’s Muse, which now has over 10 million users, has seen AI-assisted shopping become a top activity on its app. Other personal AI agents, like Instinct, also support making purchases on users’ behalf. It’s no surprise, then, that OpenAI would want to enter this space more with an agentic shopping feature of its own. The merchant will automatically receive what it needs to fulfill the order from the dot, like the shipping address and contact information, OpenAI says. The company notes that customers who shop via their dots will still be able to earn their credit card rewards and be able to take advantage of protections that typically come with cards, like being able to dispute transactions. The limited availability at launch will allow OpenAI to test and improve the feature and its capabilities before rolling it out more broadly. In the future, the company plans to offer users more control over the feature by allowing them to set spending limits or configure other parameters around purchase categories or time periods, so they can pre-approve purchases that their agent can then handle more autonomously. It also aims to make the agentic shopping feature an option at a broader number of supported retailers. This could be a challenge in some areas, where retailers are blocking AI agents from using their site ; on the shopping front, the largest retailer to ban AI agents is Amazon, as it aims to steer users to its own AI agent, Alexa, instead. To help retailers adapt to agentic commerce, OpenAI also published a Commerce Partner Playbook that offers tools and guidance to sites that want to support customers using agents. articles.title: Microsoft's latest email outage turned into a full-blown global cloud crisis | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Microsoft's daylong outage began with Outlook and Teams and ended up taking much of the company's cloud services offline. Microsoft says it's gradually restoring service.
articles.body_text: Microsoft is slowly recovering from its daylong outage after much of the company’s systems were hit by a cascading software issue. The problems, which started Thursday, were initially flagged as affecting the company’s services in the U.S. and the Americas, but quickly spread around the world, as engineers struggled to recover downed servers. What began as an Outlook email and Teams video conferencing outage soon developed into a full-blown meltdown affecting the company’s cloud services for both consumer and business email, files, and documents. The outage also knocked out the company’s Copilot AI tools and Defender security screening software, and prevented system administrators from accessing their internal Intune dashboards and features. Some users reportedly experienced issues with accessing their cloud-based Windows computers. Microsoft hasn’t yet said what caused the issues, only saying the outage involved “a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable.” The company said it continues to investigate the cause. The outage affected a broad range of industries, including TechCrunch’s own email. We’ve reached out to Microsoft for comment about the incident. As of Friday morning on the U.S. East Coast, Microsoft’s Outlook email service had begun to recover and some emails have been trickling in. The recovery comes after engineers initially could not find the cause of the issue that was causing servers in Microsoft’s data centers to fail. Doug Madory, the director of internet analysis at Kentik, a company that monitors internet traffic worldwide, said in a post on Bluesky that traffic was returning to Microsoft’s services after about 18 hours of downtime. Microsoft said in its latest status update on Friday that there was “no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident,” and later noted that there was “not related to cyber or AI / agents.” That may be some solace for the millions who went without their email and online services yesterday, but the company is likely to face questions about its inability to swiftly recover from an outage of its own making. A Microsoft spokesperson did not respond to our questions asking if the company has the technical means to detect malicious activity, such as logs, or if Microsoft has a way to check what happened. “We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure,” said Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president for Copilot, agents, and platform, in a statement on Friday. “Our teams are reviewing what happened and how we can prevent similar issues going forward.” The last major incident affecting Microsoft services was in September , when a dayslong outage hit Microsoft’s cloud services. During that outage, Microsoft blamed a “core authentication configuration” issue that prevented users from accessing the service. I en debattartikel i tidningen Syre skriver han att Vänsterpartiet , Socialdemokraterna, Miljöpartiet och Centerpartiet riskerar att förlora möjligheten att bilda regering – trots att de tillsammans har majoritet. ”Av det enkla skälet att de fyra partierna inte tycks ha förstått förhandlingens mest elementära byggsten: att ge och ta” skriver han. Enligt Jens Holm har förhandlingarna hittills handlat för lite om politik och för mycket om ministerposter. Han efterlyser i stället ett gemensamt reformprogram med bland annat klimatinvesteringar, satsningar på skola, sjukvård och billig kollektivtrafik. – Efter att Sverigedemokraterna sa att de kan stödja Kristersson som statsminister utan att kräva ministerposter har spelplanen ändrats. Det är också det som har gjort att Centern vände sig högerut, säger han och fortsätter: – Då måste de rödgröna vara flexibla, inte minst Vänsterpartiet. Att bara ha ett förhandlingskort i liksom i rockfickan – ministerposter – det är inte särskilt framgångsrikt för en förhandlingsstrategi, skulle jag säga. Vänsterpartiet ökade mest av alla partier i valet och ska självklart ha betalt för sitt fina valresultat. Men betalningen borde främst räknas i vänsterpolitik – inte ministerposter, menar Jens Holm.

Somliga kommer nu behöva sluta hoppas på något annat, någon magisk mittenlösning som ska utkristallisera sig eller att man skulle dra detta till extraval. articles.title: Demon face syndrom gör att Karl ser kattögon – hos människor
articles.summary: En hjärnoperation räddade hans liv. Men den kom med ett pris. Karl har fått demon face syndrome och ser nu kattögon – hos människor.
articles.body_text: Karl har fått demon face syndrome och ser nu kattögon – hos människor. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Är du 18–25 år? Nu kan du läsa Expressen gratis i ett år – avslutas automatiskt. Klicka här! Karl ser kattansikten på människor – och tvärtom. Efter en hjärnoperation utvecklade han den ovanliga diagnosen ”demon face syndrome”. Fallet kan ge nya svar om hur hjärnan känner igen ansikten. Prosopometamorfopsi (PMO) är en synstörning mer känd under ett annat namn: Demon face syndrome . Personer som lider av åkomman beskriver det ibland som att ansikten kan förändras till att få demonliknande drag. Men ny forskning beskriver en betydligt mer specifik form av PMO. I en studie som publicerats av Cortex berättar forskare vid Dartmouth-universitet om en person med en extremvariant av åkomman. I studien anonymiseras personen, boende i nordöstra USA, som ”Karl”. Och Karl har ett en specifik variant av PMO. I människors ansikten ser han – sin katt Luna. Detsamma gäller även omvänt att Karl ibland kan se andras ansikten i Lunas. Brad Duchaine, professor och hjärnforskare vid Dartmouth, förklarar att det förklarar en hel del om hur våra hjärnor fungerar. – Det visar att individuella anletsdrag kan hämtas från minnet och påverka vad vi ser, säger Duchaine i ett pressmeddelande om studien.

articles.title: Zelenskyjs varning: Sverige kommer tas upp
articles.summary: Rysslands president Vladimir Putin kommer ta upp Sverige – i ett försök att rubba ”Europas säkerhetsarkitektur”. Det varnar Ukrainas president Volodymyr Zelenskyj för. articles.title: Dödliga sveket – Lilla hjärtats sista tid i livet
articles.summary: I en ny bok ger Expressens kriminalkrönikör Fredrik Sjöshult hela den mörka bilden av hur flickan sveks av samhället och dödades av sina föräldrar – drogad och undernärd.
articles.body_text: Esmeralda är flickan som inte fick fylla fyra år. I en ny bok ger Expressens kriminalkrönikör Fredrik Sjöshult hela den mörka bilden av hur flickan sveks av samhället och dödades av sina föräldrar – drogad och undernärd. Här följer ett utdrag från ”Lilla hjärtat, mamman och pappan”. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Det finns en film på Esmeralda som Melinda Jacobs nu inte orkar titta på när vi ses utanför Vadstena hösten 2026. Melinda spelade in den i slutet av Esmeraldas så kallade hemsluss. Den lilla flickan står i hallen. Hon är ledsen och vill inte åka, men hon måste. Det finns inte längre någon återvändo. Jag förstår att Melinda tycker det är jobbigt av flera skäl, inte minst på grund av att hon lovat Esmeralda att skydda henne. Melinda tänker samma sak som jag när filmen kommer upp: Vad var det egentligen som hände under Esmeraldas sista tid i livet? Vad utsattes hon för hos sina biologiska föräldrar i Norrköping? Esmeralda hittades död hemma hos sina biologiska föräldrar i Norrköping i januari 2020. De greps och häktades direkt. Hon hade tvingats lämna Melinda Jacobs familjehem efter en kammarrättsdom om LVU och lämnats åt sitt öde i föräldrarnas drogmisär. När hon dog var hon undernärd och drogad. Pappan dog i häktet. Mamman dömdes senare för dråp till åtta års fängelse. Sveket mot Esmeralda, som kallats för ”Lilla hjärtat”, har tack vare Melinda Jacobs kamp resulterat i flera ändringar av lagen för att barnets bästa ska sättas i första rummet. Socialtjänsten har också fått utökade möjligheter att kräva drogtester av föräldrar och i nästa steg ska nu barnets ”anknytning” väga tyngre när beslut tas i en LVU-process. Trots att Melinda och jag setts och haft kontakt otaliga gånger genom åren har hon tidigare aldrig pratat om filmen. Men när jag nu satt punkt för boken och sätter mig ned med henne tar hon upp den.

articles.body_text: Förhandlingarna om en ny rödgrön regering är inne i ett kritiskt skede. Planen är att göra både C och V nöjda – med över hundra sakpolitiska förslag. Expressen kan nu avslöja nya detaljer från S hemliga totalplan för Sverige. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Socialdemokraternas plan är att bilda en rödgrön regering ihop med Miljöpartiet och Centerpartiet och samarbeta nära med Vänsterpartiet utanför regering. Intensiva förhandlingar har förts mellan partierna och detaljerna i S-planen för Sverige har hittills varit okända. Personer med insyn beskriver förhandlingarna som särskilt känsliga och det har varit viktigt att hålla information och underlag i en ytterst liten krets. Expressen har tagit del av planen som S presenterat för samarbetspartierna och kan berätta nya detaljer om innehållet. Dokumentet innehåller en rad förslag på hur S tilltänkta regering kan garantera Centerpartiets röda linjer mot SD och V upprätthålls samtidigt som ”mycket” av Centerns politik kan bli verklighet. Det är Socialdemokraterna som tagit fram dokumentet efter samtal och förhandlingar mellan de potentiella regeringspartierna. Man tar även upp frågor som behöver förhandlas ytterligare samt ett antal principiella frågor där det är viktigt att ”alla partier blir vinnare”. Om det här alternativet inte går i lås beskriver dokumentet hur det bara är en regering där S och M ingår ihop som har förutsättningar att fungera i praktiken utan att vara beroende av Sverigedemokraterna.

articles.title: Expressen Direkt
articles.summary: Expressens direkflöde med senaste nyheterna i korthet • Största nyhetshändelserna i Sverige och världen
articles.body_text: S-ledaren Magdalena Andersson skrev i en debattartikel i Expressen att Vänsterpartiet är redo att förhandla vidare om en rödgrön regering. Det innebär inte att V accepterat att stå utanför en rödgrön regering, skrev V-toppen Ida Gabrielsson i en kommentar. Andersson skriver nu på Instagram att hon ”får frågor” om debattartikeln. ”Det jag hänvisar till i debattartikeln är samma besked som V meddelande på pressträffen i torsdags. Att om Centerpartiet väljer att gå vidare med Socialdemokraternas förslag är Vänsterpartiet redo att delta i de fortsatta förhandlingarna. Ingenting annat.” Strax innan klockan 13 fick SOS Alarm samtal om en brand på en båt i Skärhamn på Tjörn. Nu uppger polisen att en person har dött. ”Det visar sig senare vara rökutveckling. En person har avlidit till följd av händelsen” , skriver polisen på sin hemsida. Vad som hänt är ännu oklart. Båten ska undersökas av polisens tekniker. Polisen har upprättat en anmälan om allmänfarlig vårdslöshet. Det finns ingen misstänkt i ärendet. Den avlidne personens anhöriga är underrättade. Den tyska biltillverkaren BMW återkallar 720 796 fordon i Nordamerika på grund av brandrisk. Innan reparationen utförts bör bilarna parkeras utomhus samt långt från andra fordon och byggnader. USA:s trafikmyndighet NHTSA skriver i ett uttalande att brand kan uppstå även när bilen är parkerad och avstängd. Fordonen återkallades redan 2024, då för att åtgärda vattenpumpen. Nu är en elkontakt på pumpen otillräckligt tätad och kan vid kontakt med vatten orsaka kortslutning, vilket ökar risken för brand. Enligt NHTSA känner BMW hittills till cirka tio incidenter i USA som kan bero på problemet, men inga personskador har rapporterats. 14 olika BMW-modeller berörs.
